title: Flagged at the Border
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Something about my landing card must have caught the officer's eye, because I was pulled from the queue and led to a side room without explanation.
Narrator: Nobody had done anything wrong, as far as I could tell, yet the mere act of being singled out made me feel instantly, irrationally guilty.
Narrator: [carefully] I sat there rehearsing my own itinerary in my head, as though I might somehow forget why I'd come, or where I was even staying.
Narrator: Across the room, an elderly man was being questioned far more thoroughly than I was, his passport passed between three different officials.
Narrator: [reflective] It occurred to me that the randomness of these checks is rarely as random as the system likes to claim.
Narrator: I'd never once been stopped like this on my other passport, the one issued by a wealthier, more trusted country.
Narrator: [honestly] Privilege, I realised, isn't only about money; it's also about which document you happen to be holding at a border.
Narrator: When the officer finally called my name, she asked a handful of routine questions, then apologised for the delay almost as an afterthought.
Narrator: [gently] I wanted to be angry, and part of me was, but another part recognised that her apology cost her nothing while my hour had cost me plenty.
Narrator: Walking out, I passed the elderly man again, still waiting, his shoulders slightly stooped under the fluorescent lights.
Narrator: [calmly] I caught his eye and offered a small, useless smile, the only gesture available to a stranger in that particular room.
Narrator: Later, on the train into the city, I found myself wondering how many trips are quietly reshaped by moments like that one.
Narrator: [encouraging] Not ruined, exactly, but tilted, coloured by a reminder that borders were never designed to treat every traveller equally.
Narrator: I don't have a tidy conclusion, only a resolve to notice, next time, whose passport lets them walk straight through.
Narrator: [seriously] Travel teaches you as much about the systems you move through as it does about the places you're heading to.
Narrator: I still travel constantly, and I still love it, but I no longer pretend the process is neutral for everyone.

quiz.question: Why was the narrator pulled from the queue at the border?
options: The reason was never explained to her
She was carrying prohibited items
She had the wrong visa
She argued with an officer
quiz.explanation: She was led to a side room without explanation, and never learns exactly why she was singled out.

quiz.question: What does the narrator notice about the elderly man across the room?
options: He was released immediately
He was questioned far more thoroughly than she was
He was travelling with her
He refused to answer questions
quiz.explanation: She observes that his passport was passed between three different officials, far more scrutiny than her own.

quiz.question: What realization does the narrator have about her other passport?
options: It had expired
It was fake
She had never been stopped like this on her passport from a wealthier country
She had lost it once before
quiz.explanation: She reflects that she was never stopped this way when travelling on her other, more trusted passport.

quiz.question: How does the officer behave once she finally calls the narrator's name?
options: She asks routine questions and apologises almost as an afterthought
She is hostile and accusatory
She refuses to explain anything
She detains her further
quiz.explanation: The officer asks a handful of routine questions, then apologises for the delay almost as an afterthought.

quiz.question: What conclusion does the narrator reach about travel and borders?
options: Borders were never designed to treat every traveller equally
Border checks are always fair and random
She will stop travelling entirely
Only wealthy travellers face delays
quiz.explanation: She concludes that the experience was a reminder that borders were never designed to treat every traveller equally.

quiz.question: What thought challenges the official claim that border checks are random?
options: I've been told more than once that mixing leisure with work trips looks unprofessional to some managers
I booked this room three months ago and paid in full
Within months, that single photograph had been shared thousands of times
The narrator notices that certain passports attract repeated scrutiny.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The narrator notices that certain passports attract repeated scrutiny.

quiz.question: Why does the officer's brief apology feel insufficient?
options: Once the conference starts, neither of us will have a spare moment to see anything beyond the hotel
I can have the driver waiting within ten minutes
A fisherman I'd spoken to years earlier recognised me
It costs her nothing while the delay substantially changes his journey.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: It costs her nothing while the delay substantially changes his journey.

quiz.question: What sight follows the narrator as he leaves the side room?
options: Just don't schedule anything that requires early mornings
Provided the room tomorrow is actually available, unlike tonight's, I suppose that works
An elderly traveller remains waiting beneath the harsh lights.
I asked him whether he wished I'd never taken the picture
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: An elderly traveller remains waiting beneath the harsh lights.

quiz.question: How does the experience change the narrator's understanding of privilege?
options: Now that's a trip I'd actually look forward to, rather than merely tolerate
Documents can shape freedom of movement as powerfully as money.
I'll text you the confirmation and the driver's details right away
I still photograph places I love
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Documents can shape freedom of movement as powerfully as money.

quiz.question: What resolve replaces a simple conclusion about the incident?
options: Let's just hope the client doesn't reschedule the whole conference on us again
I'd rather trust you than the booking system, honestly
The village will keep changing regardless of what I do
He will notice whose passport allows effortless passage.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He will notice whose passport allows effortless passage.
